name: ai-workbench-block
title: AI workbench block (Workbench shell + activity rail + Sources dock)
description: The `Workbench` shell as a double-column AI desk — an `ActivityRail` + `ConversationList` sidebar, a scripted `ThinkingIndicator` → `ToolCallCard` → `StreamingText` review turn, a docked `Sources` citations panel, and `PromptInput` + `ModelPicker` as the composer.
author: wmzy <https://github.com/wmzy>
docs:
The `Workbench` shell as a double-column AI desk — an `ActivityRail` + `ConversationList` sidebar, a scripted `ThinkingIndicator` → `ToolCallCard` → `StreamingText` review turn, a docked `Sources` citations panel, and `PromptInput` + `ModelPicker` as the composer. ## Install ```bash npx shadcn@latest add wmzy/haze-ui/ai-workbench-block ``` The full-page source lands at `components/block/haze/ai-workbench-block.tsx` (via the `@block/` target placeholder from `components.json`) — vendored, so you own and edit it. Component imports are rewritten to the `haze-ui` npm package, which is installed automatically together with `lucide-react` and `react-use-control`. The file imports the stylesheet of every component it renders (`haze-ui/css/tokens.css` + 20 component css files), so no extra stylesheet setup is needed. ## Theming This wrapper re-exports the 'lightTheme' (or 'darkTheme'), 'spacing' and 'typography' classes from 'haze-ui' and imports 'haze-ui/css/tokens.css'. Activate the design tokens by applying the classes to a root element: ```jsx import { lightTheme, spacing, typography } from 'haze-ui'; // on or any root container — darkTheme is a drop-in swap
…
``` Live preview and source: https://wmzy.github.io/haze-ui/#/blocks — https://github.com/wmzy/haze-ui/tree/main/registry
